concrete_findings.finding: Neet turns increasing comfort into increasingly ambitious interference: seat controls, champagne, sleeping positions, then cockpit buttons. Buddy testing the stretch twice and discovering Enough add quiet timing between larger incidents. Heather escalating one napkin into the stack is a visual reaction gag; the image pause comes before cheers and her mid-flight downgrade line, without separating dialogue from its attribution.

Neet is grandiose and delighted by his own trouble; Buddy wants reliable rest and acts toward it by testing controls, stopping, securing his blanket, calling Heather and reclaiming the blanket. Heather enjoys the meal, repairs the social mess and lifts Neet back, making her an affectionate participant. Historical Heather-and-dogs household remains intact.

Each physical incident follows Neet actively exploiting another luxury. Buddy’s final paw over the controls pays off Enough and the earlier falls; They had reached the ground is consistent with landing/taxiing. The extravagant cockpit incident is retained fictional escalation, not a factual aviation claim. Ending leaves the family together with affection beneath exasperation.

Comfort shows Buddy’s extended forepaws ending inside a roomy cushion before takeoff, with a terminal outside. Napkins shows the slow face wipe and full stack offer before Heather buries her face. Floor shows Neet already seated in the aisle, Buddy looking down and blanket displaced before Heather lifts him. No state is placed after it has ceased to apply.

The three compositions progress from Buddy’s private comfort test, to a social human reaction and sheepish Neet, to the interrupted nap with a clear vertical seat/floor relationship. They add distinct comedy rather than repeating portraits; the final button callback remains readable prose and is not crowded by a fourth image.
